reviewed_variants.label: no nontrivial open separation
reviewed_variants.text: A topological space X is connected if it cannot be written as the union of two disjoint nonempty open subsets.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: No nonempty assumption on X is required; the empty space is connected.

reviewed_variants.label: only trivial clopen subsets
reviewed_variants.text: A topological space X is connected precisely when its only subsets that are both open and closed are ∅ and X.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: For empty X, ∅=X, so the condition holds.

reviewed_variants.label: two-point discrete test
reviewed_variants.text: A topological space X is connected precisely when there is no continuous surjection from X onto the discrete two-element space.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: This is equivalent to the nontrivial-clopen condition via the preimages of the two singleton open sets.

mathematical_review: Important original-INDEPENDENT-reconstruction defect: existing meaning text begins 'A nonempty topological space X is connected if...' This unnecessarily excludes the empty topological space under the standard no-separation convention; the ProofWiki source imposes no nonempty premise. Amend this meaning in place with a full source-attributed historic correction, not a duplicate meaning; preserve its old reviewed source and link decisions. The current formulation also conflates the no-separation and clopen characterizations into one sentence; the project policy prefers separate equivalent formulations under the same heading.

reviewed_variants.label: all ideals finitely generated
reviewed_variants.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if every ideal of R is finitely generated.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: This is the standard ring-theoretic formulation.

reviewed_variants.label: ascending chain condition
reviewed_variants.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if every ascending chain of ideals I_1⊆I_2⊆⋯ stabilizes.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: Equivalent to finite generation of every ideal, with an appropriate proof.

reviewed_variants.label: maximal condition on ideals
reviewed_variants.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if each nonempty collection of ideals of R has a maximal element under inclusion.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: Equivalent to ACC when dependent choice or ordinary standard classical axioms are assumed.

reviewed_variants.label: Noetherian as module over itself
reviewed_variants.text: A commutative ring R is Noetherian if R, regarded as a left R-module over itself, is Noetherian.
reviewed_variants.mathematical_scope: The R-submodules of R are precisely its ideals; no noncommutative or one-sided conventions are silently imported.

mathematical_review: The existing independently sourced Noetherian-ring meaning has two equivalent characterizations inside one formulation. ProofWiki confirms four mathematically equivalent characterizations for commutative unital rings. Review as separate formulations under the same already screened context instead of adding another meaning. In a general noncommutative ring left/right Noetherian are distinct: do not omit commutativity if retaining the same source scope.
